text: Now let's actually aggregate real events — summarize.

Summarize by combines group by and agg into one operator — by vendor I-D is the grouping, and named aggregate expressions compute per group, the exact same idea as Foundations' agg, just KQL's own naming order.
Count, sum, average, max — genuinely the same aggregate functions from Foundations, just called with KQL's own syntax instead of Python's.

And bin is a genuinely new idea — it rounds a timestamp down to the nearest interval, so summarize by bin groups events into real time buckets. This is the real mechanism behind every time-series aggregation this chapter builds toward.
Group, aggregate, and now bucket by time — as the stream arrives, not after it's already loaded. Next lesson: KQL joins, combining tables, KQL's own way.
